data.exact_reserve_text: In 2017, there has been an overall deterioration of GBP 53.7m (2016: improvement of GBP 1.6m).

prior_year_events.event_name: Adverse claims development in short tail lines
prior_year_events.impact_description: Syndicate 1200 had to strengthen loss reserves predominantly in short tail lines of business that have seen the most rate pressure in the market over the last four years, namely US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull. These lines have seen rate reductions of up to 50% in the last 4 years as well as unsustainable losses developing well in excess of the expected level. The deterioration in these classes of business during 2017 (and to some extent 2016) led us to make certain underwriting decisions during 2017.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1200 experienced an overall gross reserve strengthening of GBP 53.7 million in 2017, primarily driven by adverse claims development in short tail lines of business, including US Direct & Facultative, Cargo, Yachts & Hull, which had experienced significant rate pressure and unsustainable losses. This deterioration affected the 2016 and prior underwriting years. The year 2017 was also significantly impacted by natural catastrophe events such as Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, and Maria, California wildfires, and Mexico earthquakes, contributing to the challenging market conditions.

data.data_quality_notes: The GBP 53.7m deterioration is stated as 'overall' and not explicitly 'gross', but is assumed gross given the context of claims provisions. This figure cannot be directly reconciled with the gross claims development triangle provided in the report, which shows a much smaller movement for prior years.
